content.comment_body: Updating [product_name] V7.0 to 7.1 and 7.1.5 worked online with the updater, but upgrading to the 32 or 64bit versions of [product_name] V8.0 completed installation yet still showed 7.1.5 as installed. The V8.0 upgrade did not work via the internet for me on three different computers: one Windows 7-64bit with the 64bit upgrade, one XP32 notebook, and another XP-32 desktop. Frustrated that the device wouldn't upload to [product_name] V7.0 or 7.1.5, I questioned if I had a demo version but confirmed it was a full copy. It continued reporting failed communication with the IP, despite being able to ping and access the device's web server (with server reported disabled). In need of the program, I found a forum message with a direct download link. After downloading and installing the 64bit version using File System, it finally worked. I was unaware that V8.0 was required for my [product_name] with [article_no], and lost a weekend trying to upload a program coded at work on a PC that already had V8.0 installed. Key points learned: 1) Make clear when software is a demo and what functions are limited. 2) Show registration status prominently, e.g. in the About tab. 3) Clearly mark on packaging that V8.0 is required for newer devices. 4) Simplify forum registration for better support since this product targets home technologies and consumers. 5) Improve error reporting and make connectivity straightforward for IoT usage, avoiding driver hassle. 6) Fix the broken web updater. 7) Make update download links easy to find, without excessive menu navigation. 8) [company_name] is too large to effectively support end users; consider creating a dedicated sub brand. 9) I would have purchased V8.0 online, but the site lacks a working vendor link. 10) [product_name] remains my favorite PLC software with FBD—please continue to improve.
The claim about updating via the internet not working is incorrect. I successfully updated online myself.

Glad it worked for you. Not sure when you updated, but I maintain my experience. I installed on three different machines this past weekend via the internet, and it was definitely broken for me. The 8.0 update completed normally without errors, but at the end, the version was still 7.1.(5?). However, the File System type update to 8.0 succeeded fully. I am updating from a V7.0 licensed distribution CD. Your experience may vary.
It may simply not be working for you for some reason, but you cannot generalize and say it does not work for everyone.

Here are a few suggestions: 1) Is your PC running a supported operating system (not Windows 10)? 2) Are you running [product_name] V7 as an administrator? (Right-click the executable, go to Properties/Compatibility, and select Run as Admin.) 3) Do you have full rights on the PC? (Test by copying a file to the C drive; if you are prompted for admin rights, you aren't an admin.) From my experience, the update works without issue over the internet. I checked again and found no problems. Hope this helps.
Slightly off topic, but I'm using V8 on Windows 10 without any problems.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report notable issues upgrading [product_name] from V7.1.5 to V8.0 online, with the installer completing but not updating the actual version on multiple systems. Compatibility problems emerge when software and device versions do not match, leading to confusion. The experience emphasizes the need for clear information regarding version requirements, clearly displayed demo versus registered status, simplified download and update navigation, better error reporting, and more accessible product guidance for consumers.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expected a smooth and reliable online update process, clear indications of version compatibility, obvious demo/registration status, simple access to update downloads, and an efficient way to purchase V8.0 software directly.
